text:
alex kim: Quick thread — proposing a combined codelab + live webinar to launch the new OSS reference app (lightweight inference example). Target: devs and community contributors, drive GH stars + demo signups. Thinking Apr 14. High-level: 20m intro, 30m walkthrough codelab, 25m benchmarking & Q&A. Thoughts?

maya singh: yes please. we should lean into a short benchmark narrative: show latency & cost improvements with default config vs optimized (batching + quant). concrete numbers win here. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

rachel ford: agree on the benchmark callout. can we also bake a tiny interactive snippet in the codelab that runs on wasm or a cheap cloud runner so folks try it in-browser? low friction is key.

samir patel: routing question — where do inbound signups go? propose: webhook -> hubspot -> deal created w/ lifecycle_stage=marketing. add tag: "oss-codelab-apr14" and lead_source=community. jess, any objections?

jess product: +1. sales ops prefers a Zapier fallback and a direct HubSpot endpoint. please ensure form includes a hidden field `utm_campaign=oss_codelab_apr14` and `utm_source=community`. also add a checkbox for "interested in dedicated/private deployment" so we flag higher intent.

alex kim: perfect. for the registration form copy I drafted: "Join our 1-hour codelab to build a lightweight inference app using Redwood's runtime — includes performance tips and a reproducible benchmark. Space limited, live Q&A." short CTA: "Reserve your spot".

maya singh: wording is good. for the blog/launch post we should have 3 hooks: 1) get started tutorial, 2) benchmark summary (2x cost reduction example), 3) community contrib path (how to open PRs to the refapp). keep hero image showing simple arch diagram + latency numbers.

rachel ford: timeline check — copy & assets ready by Apr 7, form + tracking by Apr 9, dry run w/ speakers Apr 12. can calendar-bot create the event?

calendar-bot: Event created — "Redwood OSS Codelab: Build & Benchmark" • Apr 14 • 10:00 PDT — https://calendar.redwood.example/event/12345

samir patel: for lead routing implement these HubSpot properties: `source_detail=oss_codelab`, `interest=developer`, `intent_score=auto` (default 0). we can enrich later via Clearbit. also route any high intent leads (checkbox checked) to Sales queue "Platform".

alex kim: notes for the codelab content: include a short section "Save money: batching & caching in practice" with commands:```bash
# run local benchmark
python bench.py --model gpt-small --quantize 4bit --batch 8
``` and show sample results table. keep it simple so people can replicate.

maya singh: webinar plan: MC + 2 devs (one author, one infra). MC does 5m intro, dev walkthrough 30m, infra person covers perf tuning 15m, then 10-15m Q&A. capture questions in a public GH discussion thread.

jess product: marketing ops: can we add UTM templates for partners who amplify? utm_source=partnername&utm_campaign=oss_codelab_apr14 — we'll include in partner kit. also create short share text and GIF for socials.

ops-bot: Deploy checklist created: create-form -> add-hubspot-webhook -> add-utm-params -> analytics tag -> blog post scheduled. Assignee: @alex kim.

rachel ford: can someone own a small post-webinar survey (2 questions + NPS)? use it to capture whether they tried the codelab and if they want a dedicated trial.

samir patel: tagging convention in HS: `campaign_slug:oss_codelab_apr14`, `channel:webinar`, `lead_team:platform`. I'll add automation rules after first 50 signups.

alex kim: OK I'll own content + slides. @maya can you own benchmark writeup and GH demo? @jess can you handle ops & routing? I'll drop a draft of the blog + registration form by EOD Apr 4.

maya singh: yes, will get the mini-bench done and a reproducible script.

jess product: on it — will set up Zapier and HubSpot mappings and post back the webhook test payload here.

alex kim: thanks all. small action items in the checklist — let's use this thread for quick updates. :rocket:
